transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, hi. Thanks. Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, it's the nights. Most nights, when my wife goes to bed—she's a really heavy sleeper, actually. She works these crazy long shifts, so once her head hits the pillow, she is out cold. We actually bought one of those fancy white noise machines a few years back, but she doesn't even need it. I'm the one who ends up listening to the ocean sounds. 

But anyway, once she's asleep, I always end up in the kitchen. And I just... I eat way past a normal plate. Like, recently we had all this fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls... it was leftovers from this big family reunion event thing. My aunt organized it, and she always over-orders from this catering place downtown. I actually used to go to that place all the time back when I was taking some classes at the community college, before I stopped working. They have this huge neon sign in the window, you really can't miss it. 

But yeah, I'll just be in the kitchen with whatever event leftovers are in there, and I just keep going until a whole tray or, like, half the fridge is just completely gone.

Can you tell me more about these episodes in the kitchen? Specifically, do you find yourself eating a noticeably larger amount of food than what most people would eat in a similar period of time, and do you feel like you can’t stop yourself once you start?

Yeah, it's definitely way more than a normal person would eat. We actually have these really big dinner plates, too. My wife bought them at a yard sale a couple of streets over a few years ago. The neighbors were moving down to Florida—Tampa, I think, because the husband got some job at a marine biology center or an aquarium or something. Anyway, they had these huge plates with little blue flowers painted around the edges, and we bought the whole set for like ten bucks. Such a steal. 

But, um, yeah... with the food, it's like... once I take that first bite, it feels like the decision has already been made for me. I'll just be standing there in the kitchen—which gets really drafty at night, by the way, I keep meaning to fix the weather stripping on the back door since I have the time now—but even while I’m standing there telling myself, 'George, stop now,' my hands just have a mind of their own. They just keep fixing another one of those blue flower plates, or opening another Tupperware container. I just... I can't make myself stop.

latest_inference.note: The patient describes recurrent episodes of eating significantly more food than most people would consume in a similar timeframe, coupled with a sense of loss of control once eating begins. This aligns with the core features of binge eating disorder. No other disorders are strongly indicated at this point, and there is insufficient evidence to support additional diagnoses.
